transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees (Redwood): Jordan Patel, Maya Lin, Connor Hayes
Attendees (BluePeak): Evan Ruiz, Priya Shah, Marcus Lee, Olivia Grant

Summary:
Quick alignment between procurement and legal on MSA/DPA redlines, pricing approval lanes, and SLA tiering for a pilot to start in March. Technical runbook and network preflight required before pilot sign-off.

Topics covered:
- MSA redline process and who signs circles
- DPA exceptions (data residency, retention, logging)
- SLA tiers and credits/penalties model for Dedicated vs Hosted
- Pricing bands and pilot discounting vs committed capacity
- Technical preflight: VPC peering, KMS, firewall, KV cache behavior

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick roll call before we start — Jordan from Redwood, Maya and Connor here.
[00:12] Evan Ruiz: Evan from BluePeak, Priya, Marcus and Olivia on our side.
[00:16] Jordan Patel: Awesome, perfect. Our goal today is to stitch together the legal and commercial asks with the tech bits so we can get a clean pilot sign-off window. We're hoping, as discussed over email, to get pilot in early March.
[00:30] Priya Shah: Yeah, we got the initial MSA and DPA, looked through them. We have about a handful of DPA exceptions around data residency and audit log retention, and a couple of MSA clauses on liability that need alignment.
[00:42] Maya Lin: Totally expected — do you want me to run through the technical side so we can map which items are contractual versus operational?
[00:49] Priya Shah: That would help. Also can you point to the attestation docs you mentioned?
[00:53] Jordan Patel: Yep, I'll drop the SOC2/ISO attestation in the follow-up, plus a network diagram. For today, Maya maybe give a 6-minute tech sketch on deployment modes and SLA behavior?
[01:03] Maya Lin: Sure. So high level: Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC) — for BluePeak pilot you said you wanted an isolated footprint but with lower time-to-value, so we're leaning Dedicated with VPC peering. In Dedicated, we provide reserved GPU pools, and you can pin model versions. SLA differs: Hosted has best-effort tiers, Dedicated has committed throughput and latency targets, and Private has the strictest isolation controls.
[01:31] Marcus Lee: Quick question — when you say KV cache, is that inside our VPC or on Redwood runtime? We need to know where PII could show up.
[01:38] Maya Lin: Good question. The KV cache is runtime-managed; for Dedicated with VPC peering we can ensure the cache persists in the runtime instance that lives in the customer's tenancy — but the short version is we can honor in-flight caching that doesn't persist to external storage.
[01:51] Marcus Lee: Ok, so we still need to know retention windows and whether we can disable prefix caching for some routes.
[01:56] Connor Hayes: We can absolutely disable prefix/KV caching per route; that will affect token cost and latency slightly, we'll document that tradeoff in the runbook.
[02:04] Priya Shah: And KMS? We need to know whether keys are customer-managed.
[02:08] Jordan Patel: For Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; for Dedicated we have options — you can bring your own key for egress encryption and some of the storage artifacts. We'll clarify which artifacts are covered.
[02:19] Evan Ruiz: From procurement point, I want clarity on SLAs. Our lead concern is availability and latency percentiles for our customer-facing features. What does a typical SLA clause look like and what are the credits?
[02:30] Maya Lin: Example: For Dedicated we target 99.9% availability per month with latencies measured at p95. Credits are scaled by downtime buckets — e.g., 10% credit for 0.5 - 1 hour, 25% for 1-4 hours. We're flexible on service credits and also offer fallbacks to lower-cost model variants when capacity is constrained.
[02:51] Olivia Grant: And can the SLA be tied to model version pinning? We need deterministic behavior during a release window.
[02:56] Connor Hayes: Yes, model pinning is supported. If you pin a model we guarantee the pinned variant will be available unless you request a version rollout. Rollouts can be controlled via canary/A-B rules in the console.
[03:07] Priya Shah: For liability and indemnity, our standard counsel asks for data breach clauses and a cap on liability aligned to the contract value. Are you able to reconcile that?
[03:17] Jordan Patel: We've seen that and our legal team can propose language. Typically Redwood has a liability cap tied to the prior 12 months fees; we can discuss if that needs to be higher for BluePeak. We'll submit a redline.
[03:28] Evan Ruiz: On pricing — we need committed capacity numbers for the pilot and a clear path to a tiered discount as we hit usage bands. Also how burst capacity works.
[03:38] Jordan Patel: For pilots we usually do a 60-day sandbox with a pilot discount — 20% off list for committed usage up to X tokens, and we include a small amount of burst capacity. After pilot, production pricing is usage-based with Commitment tiers for Dedicated. I'll include an example pricing sheet in the follow-up.
[03:57] Marcus Lee: Are egress fees a thing? If we do VPC peering?
[04:01] Connor Hayes: With VPC peering there are cloud-provider egress costs that vary by region; Redwood does not markup cloud egress for peered traffic, but your finops team will see the cloud egress line item. We can model this in the pricing spreadsheet.
[04:13] Priya Shah: On DPA items: data residency — BluePeak requires EU-residency for EU customers and cannot replicate logs to US without a legal basis. Is that configurable?
[04:23] Maya Lin: Yes, we support region pinning. For Dedicated you can pick region(s) for deployment and opt out of cross-region replication. We'll show how audit logs can be stored in-region and how long they persist.
[04:35] Olivia Grant: We also need to know about access controls — RBAC, SSO.
[04:38] Jordan Patel: Redwood Console supports SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC; we can map roles to your internal groups. We'll include a sample role matrix.
[04:48] Evan Ruiz: A practical ask — we need a clean paper trail and timeline: send redline, legal review, pilot sign-off milestone date. If we can commit to pilot starting March 10th, what do you need?
[04:58] Jordan Patel: If pilot target is March 10, we need the signed pilot SOW and the network preflight completed one week prior. So ideally SOW signed by March 3, runbook and connectivity tested by March 3-6, pilot starts March 10.
[05:12] Priya Shah: We'll try to accelerate legal review but I'll have to table exceptions. If you can send a suggested cap and the exact SLA credit table, that'll speed us up.
[05:20] Jordan Patel: Will do. I'll also call out DPA items in the redline.
[05:24] Marcus Lee: For technical preflight: we'll need a connectivity checklist — firewall ports, CIDR ranges, ingress/egress, KMS key ARNs, and any ephemeral port requirements for the runtime. Also, are you offering pull-based connectors or do we push via private link?
[05:39] Maya Lin: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink for AWS, and equivalent private connectivity in other clouds. We'll include the specific ports and CIDRs. For KMS we'll need the key policy to allow encryption/decryption from Redwood's service account identifier — we'll document the exact principals.
[05:56] Olivia Grant: Is there a standard SOW template for pilots?
[05:59] Jordan Patel: Yes, we have a pilot SOW template — I'll attach it. It includes scope, success criteria, SLAs for pilot, and an exit criteria.
[06:07] Evan Ruiz: Good. On commercial approvals — we have a pricing committee cycle next Thursday; if we can get the redline and pricing before COB Tuesday, we can attempt to push it through.
[06:16] Jordan Patel: Understood — we'll prioritize.
[06:18] Priya Shah: Quick follow on: audit logs — you mentioned retention. What are default retention policies and can we request longer retention in contract?
[06:27] Connor Hayes: Default is 90 days for request logs and 365 days for full audit logs in Dedicated, but we can negotiate longer retention as an add-on. Note increased retention may increase storage costs.
[06:37] Marcus Lee: For privacy, is there a delete API for logs and data residues? We need an ability to purge test data post-pilot.
[06:43] Maya Lin: Yes, there's a delete workflow and we can coordinate an offboard scrub in the runbook. We'll include retention and purge SLAs.
[06:51] Priya Shah: Ok that helps. A few small items — can you surface the certified sub-processors? My team wants the list of sub-processors for the DPA.
[06:58] Jordan Patel: I'll include the sub-processor list and our SOC2 report redaction as attachments.
[07:04] Evan Ruiz: Anything else from the BluePeak side?
[07:06] Olivia Grant: Not from product. We'll want a success criteria doc for the pilot that ties to latency percentiles and error rate thresholds.
[07:12] Connor Hayes: We'll author a short success criteria doc with p50/p95/p99 targets and error-rate thresholds that will be included in the SOW.
[07:20] Jordan Patel: Great. Let's do a quick recap and owners.
[07:22] Jordan Patel: Action: Jordan to send redline + pricing sheet (by Mar 2). Maya to send runbook and pilot topology (by Mar 5). Marcus to provide infra & firewall details (by Mar 3). Priya to return DPA exceptions (by Mar 4). Connor to draft success criteria portion of SOW (by Mar 2).
[07:44] Priya Shah: That timeline should work; we may request one minor DPA clause change but we'll try to keep it tight.
[07:50] Evan Ruiz: If you can get the pricing and credits table to our procurement channel thread, I'll push for approval.
[07:55] Jordan Patel: Will do. We'll also include a short appendix that maps each legal ask to an operational control so you can pass it to infosec.
[08:04] Marcus Lee: One last technical note — if we disable KV caching for certain routes, do you still support batching optimizations?
[08:10] Maya Lin: Yes, you can disable prefix caching but still benefit from request batching at the runtime level; there are tradeoffs we'll document (slightly higher per-token compute or latency variability).
[08:20] Olivia Grant: Thanks all.
[08:22] Jordan Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the attachments. End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears (e.g., KV cache referenced as "kay vee cash" early in notes), speaker labels approximate; timestamps are at irregular intervals to reflect natural conversation.

Shared artifacts referenced:
- MSA initial draft (link sent via email)
- DPA draft (link sent via email)
- SOC2 and ISO attestations (will be attached by Jordan)
- Pilot SOW template (Jordan to attach)
- Pricing sheet / commit tiers (Jordan to attach)

End of transcript.
